# omni_user_attribute (Resource)

Manages a custom user attribute definition. Requires an organization API key.

An attribute is what an access filter keys off, so this is usually the first thing a row-level security setup needs and the last thing to remove.

**Destroying this removes the value every user holds for the attribute.** It also breaks model SQL and embed SSO URLs that reference it by name, and any connection selecting an environment by its value falls back to the default environment. None of that is reported by the destroy, which succeeds.

Omni's own attributes (`omni_user_id`, `omni_user_email` and the rest) are system defined and cannot be managed here. Use the `omni_user_attribute` data source to reference one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "omni_user_attribute" "region" {
  # Reference name, used in model SQL and in embed SSO URL parameters. Letters,
  # numbers and underscores, starting with a letter, and never "omni_".
  name = "region"

  # Display name in the UI. Must not start with "Omni", and must not be one of
  # the reserved connection labels such as Host, Database or Schema.
  label       = "Region"
  description = "Sales region, used by the access filter on the orders topic."

  type          = "String"
  default_value = "anz"
}

resource "omni_user_attribute" "cost_centres" {
  name            = "cost_centres"
  label           = "Cost centres"
  type            = "String"
  multiple_values = true

  # Use default_values with multiple_values, and default_value without.
  # Setting both is rejected at plan time.
  default_values = ["unassigned"]
}

resource "omni_user_attribute" "spend_limit" {
  name  = "spend_limit"
  label = "Spend limit"
  type  = "Number"

  # Numbers are given as strings so that values beyond 2^53 - 1 keep their
  # precision, which is also how Omni stores them.
  default_value = "25000"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `label` (String) Display name shown in the Omni UI. Unique among custom attributes. Must not start with `Omni`, and must not be one of the reserved connection labels: `Host`, `Password`, `Database`, `Port`, `Schema`, `Connection Name`.
- `name` (String) Reference name used in model SQL and in embed SSO URL parameters. Must start with a letter, hold only letters, numbers and underscores, and must not start with `omni_`.

  Renaming is allowed and happens in place, but every reference to the old name breaks: model SQL, embed URLs and anything else naming it. Terraform cannot see those, so a rename here is a change to make deliberately.
- `type` (String) `String` or `Number`. Immutable: changing it replaces the attribute, which destroys every user's value for it.

### Optional

- `default_value` (String) Value used when a user has none set, for a single-valued attribute. Conflicts with `default_values`.

  A `Number` attribute takes its default here as a string, which is how Omni stores numbers so that values beyond 2^53 - 1 keep their precision.
- `default_values` (List of String) Values used when a user has none set, for an attribute with `multiple_values = true`. Conflicts with `default_value`.
- `description` (String) What the attribute is for. An empty string is stored as null.
- `multiple_values` (Boolean) Whether the attribute holds more than one value per user.

  `false` to `true` is an update. `true` to `false` is not: the API refuses it, so Terraform replaces the attribute instead, which destroys every user's value. The plan shows that replacement rather than failing during apply.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The definition's unique ID. Reference attributes by this rather than by name.
- `system` (Boolean) Always false here. System attributes are Omni's own and cannot be created or managed.
